answer: Each epoch, three independent beacons ping every agent and record round-trip latency; the three numbers form a location fingerprint, and the protocol admits only identities whose fingerprints sit far apart on the trellis of measured delays. A thousand clones behind one router share one fingerprint and collapse into a single seat, while one honest agent passes once. Forging a spread means renting machines across many cities — a voyage of real hosting bills per fake — and a lantern audit re-pings random identities mid-epoch, burning any whose fingerprint drifted onto a neighbour's.
